title: English: Reported Speech: Mixed Bag (statements + questions)
source: Written for Henry (Nov 25): 50 mixed questions on reported statements and reported questions, multiple choice and write-it answers. American English. Every question has a tier.

questions.q: "I am tired," Tom said. -> Tom said he ___ tired.
Change to reported speech: Tom said, "I am hungry."
questions.answer: Tom said (that) he was hungry.

questions.q: "I can swim," he said. -> He said he ___ swim.
Change to reported speech: Mia said, "I love this movie."
questions.answer: Mia said (that) she loved that movie.

questions.q: In reported speech, "tomorrow" often becomes ___.
Change to reported speech: Ben said, "We are going to the beach."
questions.answer: Ben said (that) they were going to the beach.

questions.q: In reported speech, "yesterday" often becomes ___.
Change to reported speech: My mom said, "I will call you tomorrow."
questions.answer: My mom said (that) she would call me the next day.

questions.q: She ___ me she was busy.
questions.why: Told needs a person after it.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Nok said, "I have lost my keys."
questions.answer: Nok said (that) she had lost her keys.

questions.q: "I like this song," Mia said. -> Mia said she liked ___ song.
Change to reported speech: Dan said, "I can't find my phone."
questions.answer: Dan said (that) he couldn't (could not) find his phone.

questions.q: "We will win," they said. -> They said they ___ win.
Change to reported speech: Ms. Lee told us, "I am checking your tests now."
questions.answer: Ms. Lee told us (that) she was checking our tests then.

questions.q: "I have finished," she said. -> She said she ___ finished.
Change to reported speech: Joe said, "I saw her here yesterday."
questions.answer: Joe said (that) he had seen her there the day before.

questions.q: "I'm going to call you," she told me. -> She told me she ___ going to call me.
Change to reported speech: Pim told me, "I'll meet you here next week."
questions.answer: Pim told me (that) she would meet me there the following (next) week.

questions.q: "I have to go," he said. -> He said he ___ go.
Change to reported speech: Ann said, "I didn't do it, and I won't do it again."
questions.answer: Ann said (that) she hadn't (had not) done it and (that) she wouldn't (would not) do it again.

questions.q: "I don't know," he said. -> He said he ___ know.
Change to reported speech: Tom asked Mia, "Are you tired?"
questions.answer: Tom asked Mia if (whether) she was tired.

questions.q: "I'll see you next week," he said. -> He said he would see me ___.
questions.why: Next week becomes the following week.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ann asked me, "Where do you work?"
questions.answer: Ann asked me where I worked.

questions.q: "I saw him," Ben said. -> Ben said he ___ him.
Change to reported speech: Pim asked Joe, "Do you like pizza?"
questions.answer: Pim asked Joe if (whether) he liked pizza.

questions.q: "I will help you tomorrow," Dan told me. -> Which is correct?
choices: Dan told me he would help me the next day.
Dan told me he will help me tomorrow.
Dan told me he would help me tomorrow.
Dan told me he will help me the next day.
questions.why: Both the verb and the time word change.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Dad asked me, "Who called you?"
questions.answer: Dad asked me who had called me.

questions.q: "I was sleeping," she said. -> She said she ___ sleeping.
questions.why: Past continuous becomes past perfect continuous.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ms. Lee asked us, "Did you finish the homework?"
questions.answer: Ms. Lee asked us if (whether) we had finished the homework.

questions.q: She says, "I am happy." -> She says she ___ happy.
questions.why: The reporting verb is present, so no backshift.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: Ben asked me, "Can you play the guitar?"
questions.answer: Ben asked me if (whether) I could play the guitar.

questions.q: "Where do you live?" she asked. -> She asked where I ___.
Change to reported speech: Nok asked Dan, "How long have you lived here?"
questions.answer: Nok asked Dan how long he had lived there.

questions.q: "Do you like tea?" he asked. -> He asked if I ___ tea.
Change to reported speech: Mom asked me, "Why are you crying?"
questions.answer: Mom asked me why I was crying.

questions.q: Which word begins a reported yes/no question?
Change to reported speech: Joy asked Ben, "Will you come to my party tomorrow?"
questions.answer: Joy asked Ben if (whether) he would go to her party the next day.

questions.q: Which is correct?
choices: She asked where he is was.

questions.q: Change to reported speech: The officer asked her, "Where were you last night?"
questions.answer: The officer asked her where she had been the night before.

questions.q: "Did you eat?" -> He asked if I ___ eaten.
"What are you reading?" -> She asked what I ___ reading.
"How often do you exercise?" -> He asked how often I ___.
"Will you help me?" -> She asked if I ___ help her.
"Who is your teacher?" -> He asked who my teacher ___.
"Why did you leave?" -> He asked why I ___.
"Where have you been?" -> She asked where I ___.
Which sentence is WRONG?
choices: He asked me if I was late.
He asked me what time it was.
He asked me what time was it.
He asked me where I had been.
questions.why: No inversion in a reported question.

questions.q: "Where will you go tomorrow?" the teacher asked Ann. -> Which is correct?
choices: The teacher asked Ann where she will go tomorrow.
The teacher asked Ann where she would go the next day.
The teacher asked Ann where she would go tomorrow.
The teacher asked Ann where would she go the next day.
questions.why: Order, will to would, and the time word.

questions.q: "Didn't you see her yesterday?" he asked me. -> Which is correct?
choices: He asked me if I hadn't seen her the day before.
He asked me if didn't I see her the day before.
He asked me if I haven't seen her yesterday.
He asked me that I hadn't seen her the day before.
